newsitem.title: JAPAN: DKB to submit sokaiya report by end of May -- BOJ.
newsitem.headline: DKB to submit sokaiya report by end of May -- BOJ.

text.p: Bank of Japan (BOJ) Governor Yasuo Matsushita told a parliamentary committee on Monday that the central bank expects Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd to submit a report on its links with a sokaiya racketeer by the end of May.
Asked if the BOJ plans to conduct a special inspection of DKB, Matsushita said the central bank would "deal with the issue properly after it examines the contents of the expected report".
Top executives of DKB, Japan's third-largest bank, resigned on Friday and the bank admitted it had been unable to cut its ties to racketeers in a widening saga of dubious deals and illegal payoffs.

DKB executives revealed the bank's misdeeds and a possible earlier attempt to hide them from regulators at a news conference on Friday after the bank announced that president Katsuhiko Kondo and chairman Tadashi Okuda would step down over the scandal.

The scandal also involves the country's biggest brokerage, Nomura Securities Co Ltd. Nomura's president and 15 other top Nomura executives have already resigned over alleged illegal payoffs to the corporate extortionist, or sokaiya, at the heart of the affair.
DKB's Kondo said the bank had made a total of 26 billion yen in loans to Yoshinori Koike, the younger brother of Ryuichi Koike, the racketeer at the heart of the Nomura scandal.
But he said the bank had believed it was making the loans to the younger Koike and his company.
Prosecutors suspect that Ryuichi Koike was given financial favours by both DKB and Nomura to prevent disruption of their shareholders' meetings by sensitive questions.
Japan's Commercial Code bans such payments.
